page: Amazon Web Services m9g.medium is a general-purpose server instance powered by a single-core AWS Graviton ARMv9 processor utilizing the Neoverse-V3 microarchitecture running at 3.3 GHz. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, this arm64 instance features 1 dedicated physical core with 1 thread, 4.0 GB of system memory, and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. The CPU cache configuration consists of a 64 KB L1d cache, a 2 MB L2 cache, and a 48 MB L3 cache, with hardware support for AES cryptography.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-threaded and multi-threaded capabilities. Single-threaded performance is strong in specific tasks, with gzip compression reaching 36.08 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression achieving a top-tier 17.04 GB/sec. However, due to its single-core limitation, multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU scores fall into the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth is mixed, with uncached large-block reads performing at an average 43.27 GB/sec, while cached small-block reads and large-block writes are relatively poor.

The primary tradeoff of the m9g.medium is its single-core architecture, which limits its utility for parallelized workloads, as evidenced by weak database operations and static web serving throughput. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for lightweight, single-threaded applications, basic utility scripting, and low-concurrency web serving where high memory density is not required. It also supports basic LLM text generation for small 135M models at an average speed of 85.02 tokens/sec, though prompt processing remains slow.
